messages.author: 3ea57457192f4f3b
messages.subject: Re: RApache qplot not working while plot does
parts:
Oh I didn't notice the Segmentation fault yet. That looks nasty. Could
be a problem in R or RApache. Did you compile R yourself or did you
grab some binary? You can try reinstalling the packages and recompile
rapache.

There were some problems in the past with older distributions, but
those got resolved when upgrading to more recent distro's. See e.g:
https://groups.google.com/forum/?fromgroups=#!searchin/rapache/%22segmentation$20fault%22/rapache/kf9qO60xM-g/IoxMlvdNHF8J

I don't think a lot of people use rapache (or R for that matter) on
suse, so you're a bit in unexplored territory. I have tested rapache
myself on Debian, Ubuntu and CentOS, so if possible I would recommend
switching to either of these.

messages.subject: Re: RApache qplot not working while plot does
parts:
Le mercredi 14 novembre 2012 22:47:11 UTC+1, Jeroen a écrit :
Oh I didn't notice the Segmentation fault yet. That looks nasty. Could
be a problem in R or RApache.

This seems to be strictly a problem in RApache and not in R, when in R be it the SuSE's binary version (accessed by /usr/lib64/R/bin/R) or the newly compiled shared library version (accessed by R or /usr/local/lib64/R/bin/R) the qplot (from ggplot2) is produced correctly.

Did you compile R yourself or did you
grab some binary? You can try reinstalling the packages and recompile
rapache.

I reinstalled R  compiled from source and as a shared library (using ./configure --enable-R-shlib, followed by make and make install). It has been placed in the /usr/local/lib64 directory (which is different than the one for the binary distribution packaged by SuSE that remains in /urs/lib64)

I then recompiled and installed RApache from the latest source distribution using
./configure \
    --with-R=/usr/local/lib64/R/bin/R \
    --with-apache2-apxs=/usr/sbin/apxs2
make
make install

This replaces the previous version of RApache in /usr/lib64/apache2/mod_R.so which I had compiled against the binary and probabily static version of R that came with SuSE.

Unfortunately nothing changed.

There were some problems in the past with older distributions, but
those got resolved when upgrading to more recent distro's. See e.g:
https://groups.google.com/forum/?fromgroups=#!searchin/rapache/%22segmentation$20fault%22/rapache/kf9qO60xM-g/IoxMlvdNHF8J

Thanks for this link but still no success. I had hoped that by compiling R as a shared library my troubles would be gone as it is the case on my MacbookAir OS X where the shared ( dynamic) library is the normal way to build R on that platform.

I don't think a lot of people use rapache (or R for that matter) on
suse, so you're a bit in unexplored territory. I have tested rapache
myself on Debian, Ubuntu and CentOS, so if possible I would recommend
switching to either of these.
I might think migrating to Ubuntu in the future although I like SuSE's powerful installation and configuration program yast

messages.subject: Re: RApache qplot not working while plot does
parts:
Have you tried changing the code in different ways, like using a device other than png?  Doing so might help you isolate what's causing the problem?

If you know your way around Linux, you could also set up Apache to dump it's core memory to a file and look at the stack trace with a debugger like gdb.  Google probably has lots of answers for the steps you need to take to do that.

Regards,

Nick

messages.subject: Re: RApache qplot not working while plot does

If the same R code works on Mac OS, and if other people are able to run your code, too, then the problem most likely has to do with the SUSE environment itself. If you really need to figure out what's causing the segmentation fault, the shortest path is probably to read about how to configure Apache on SUSE to dump core, and read about how to get a stack trace from the core file using gdb.  Other than that, there's probably not much else people can say, except to use something other than SUSE.

Regards,

Nick
